chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) saw a woman in one of the ceremonial precincts of Makkah and was impressed by her, so he proposed to her and married her, and she stayed with him. He had a friend among the Ansar who was distressed by his marriage to that woman, so he asked about her and was informed that she was from the family of Dhī al-Jadayn from the Banu Shayban in a prestigious household among her clan. So he turned to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) and said: 'May Allah make me your ransom! Your marriage to this woman was continually occupying my thoughts, and I said: Ali ibn al-Husayn has married an unknown woman, and people are also saying this. So I kept asking about her until I knew her and found her in her people's household as a Shaybaniyyah.' So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said to him: 'I used to consider you to have better judgement than what I now see. Verily, Allah brought Islam, and through it He raised the lowly one, perfected the deficient one, and ennobled [people] from blame. Hence, there is no blame upon the Muslim; rather, the blame is [that of] ignorance.'

key_terms.آلِ ذِي الْجَدَيْنِ: Family of the Two Honors (a title for the Banu Shayban)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on tribal lineage and social status in marriage according to Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the transition from pre-Islamic tribal arrogance (*Jahiliyyah*) to Islamic egalitarianism, where Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) validates a marriage based on personal merit rather than lineage. The narrative underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *Karamah* (nobility) being derived from faith and character, effectively nullifying the social stigma of marrying a woman of unknown or lower tribal standing. It serves as a practical demonstration of how Islam 'completes the deficient' by elevating individuals regardless of their ancestral pedigree.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 11.Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar (a) who said,

“ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (a) saw a lady in one of the ceremonial precincts of Makkah and was impressed by her. He thus proposed to her and married her, and she stayed with him. He had a friend among the Anṣār who was distressed by his marriage to this woman, so he asked about her and was informed that she was from the family of Dhī al-Jaddayn from the Banī Shaybān in a prestigious household among her clan. So he went to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (a) and said, ‘May Allah make me your ransom! Your marriage to this woman was continually occupying my thoughts, and I said to myself: ʿAlī ibn al- Ḥusayn has married an unknown woman, and this is something that people are also saying. So I kept asking about her until I found out who she was and came to know that she is from the clan of Shaybāniyyah.’ So ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (a) said to him, ‘I used to consider you to be someone with a better judgement than what I now see. Verily Allah sent Islam and through it He raised the lowly one, perfected the deficient one, and ennobled [the people] from rebuke [and false accusation]. Hence, there is no [undue criticism or] blame upon the Muslim; rather, the blame is only [for] ignorance.’”
